patients.label: 17-year-old right-hand-dominant male football player with left middle finger FDS avulsion and PIP fracture-dislocation
attribution_limitations: Discussion calls the injury one in which both tendons and the joint are injured, while the case text reports an intact FDP.

Introduction attributes the fracture-dislocation to a likely concurrent axial load and dorsal-directed force during a tackle event, while the case presentation describes the finger caught in another player’s jersey.
Table 1 prints no unit for the finger joint measurements.

The follow-up paragraphs sit under section headings naming two-week and six-week visits, but headings are not quotable segment text; only the Figure 3 caption states six-week postoperative imaging, which the text cites for union. Visit times and the order of the two visits are not otherwise stated.

The Table 1 first therapy session date appears to precede the burned-in study timestamps on the preoperative (Figure 1) radiographs, although the text describes therapy and orthosis use postoperatively.
The operative text says the FDS insertion site was on the distal phalanx; the article does not reconcile this with the usual middle-phalanx FDS insertion.
